title: Dynamic Balance: How Entropy Governs the Balance Between Order and Chaos in Cosmic Evolution
description: Conceptual EFC paper arguing that entropy acts as a universal regulator balancing local order formation (e.g., via gravitational collapse) against global disorder. It links the arrow of time, cosmic structure formation, and the universe’s accelerating expansion to entropy-driven energy flows within time-space.

key_results.main_finding: Entropy regulates a dynamic balance between local order creation and global disorder, setting the arrow of time and shaping cosmic evolution, structure formation, and expansion.

kill_criteria: KC1: Robust observational evidence of a sustained net decrease of entropy in an isolated macroscopic cosmic region over cosmological timescales without compensating increases elsewhere.

KC2: Measurements of star/galaxy formation demonstrating no net export or production of entropy to the surroundings (e.g., radiation, turbulence, neutrinos), implying local order is achieved without global entropy increase.
KC3: High-precision CMB or early-universe probes showing the initial conditions were not low-entropy relative to later epochs, contradicting the claimed entropy-defined arrow of time.
KC4: Empirical observation of macroscopic time-asymmetric processes proceeding opposite to the entropy gradient (i.e., a reversed arrow of time) in natural cosmic settings.

KC5: Cosmological analyses demonstrating that the universe’s accelerating expansion is fully decoupled from entropy production (e.g., acceleration persists unchanged while the cosmic entropy production rate trends to zero across epochs).
